name: Old Norse Ymir creation complex
source_label: Eddic Ymir material in Poetic Edda and Snorri's Prose Edda

earliest_written_attestation.note: Snorri Sturluson's Prose Edda was probably composed c. 1221–1225 and preserves a coherent prose synthesis of Norse creation material.

surviving_manuscript_date.note: The Codex Regius manuscript of the Poetic Edda was copied around 1270 and preserves mythological poems used alongside the Prose Edda; the oldest Prose Edda manuscript is early 14th century.

tradition_internal_claim.note: The sources describe primordial Ginnungagap/Ymir and world formation rather than a historical date.

estimated_oral_origin.method: Many Eddic myths likely circulated before their surviving manuscripts, but the date and form of earlier oral narratives are contested and cannot be recovered precisely.

dating.dating_summary: The surviving written witnesses are medieval Icelandic and postdate Scandinavian Christianization. The Ymir material includes older eddic poetry plus Snorri's 13th-century synthesis; earlier oral antiquity is acknowledged but not fake-dated.

notes: The record preserves source criticism: Snorri combines and systematizes older material and should not be treated as a transparent transcript of one pre-Christian canonical narrative.
